## Who may do what

For each action, the combinations `sekisho check` walked, put together where Cedar answers them alike and the same policies decide. Rows that differ in one column only are one row, the column holding their values: `any` is every value the column takes, `not …` every value but one. `-` is a column that does not apply to the row (the roles of a workflow, say).

### action `read_order`

Look at an order

- It guards no operation.
- Principals: `User`. Resources: `Order`.
- Computed: `kind` (under Computed values below).
- 4 combinations, 2 of them allowed.

> [!NOTE]
> Some combinations of this action rest on a value another language could not say can happen, and are counted in case it can; the tables below hold them too (see What check warns of).

#### Allowed

| principal | clerk | kind | Deciding policies |
|---|---|---|---|
| User | yes | other | clerks_read |
| User | yes | odd_half | clerks_read, halves_read |

#### Denied

- No permit applies to the 2 combinations that are denied.

## Policies

Each policy as the `.gate` writes it, beside the Cedar `sekisho gen --target cedar` generates for it. A permit allows the combinations it applies to; a forbid denies those it applies to, and wins where a permit applies too. Cedar denies a combination no policy applies to. A condition on a rule's answer names the value as the `.rule` writes it (`odd_half`) in the `.gate`, and as the string Cedar is given (`"odd_half"`) in the Cedar.

### permit `clerks_read`

A clerk reads

- On `read_order`, it allows 2 combinations; no other permit allows 1 of them.

`tests/mutants/W303_a_value_no_input_reaches.gate`

```gate
permit clerks_read
  description "A clerk reads"
  principal in clerk
  action read_order
```

`cedar/halves.cedar`

```cedar
@id("halves/clerks_read")
@doc("A clerk reads")
permit (
  principal in Halves::Role::"clerk",
  action == Halves::Action::"read_order",
  resource is Halves::Order
);
```

### permit `halves_read`

Whoever is at one and a half twice reads

- On `read_order`, it allows 1 combination, which another permit allows too.

`tests/mutants/W303_a_value_no_input_reaches.gate`

```gate
permit halves_read
  description "Whoever is at one and a half twice reads"
  principal in clerk
  action read_order
  when kind is odd_half
```

`cedar/halves.cedar`

```cedar
@id("halves/halves_read")
@doc("Whoever is at one and a half twice reads")
permit (
  principal in Halves::Role::"clerk",
  action == Halves::Action::"read_order",
  resource is Halves::Order
)
when { context.kind == "odd_half" };
```

## Computed values

What an action computes and gives Cedar in its context. The generated code computes each one from the service's own data, the operation's arguments and the server's clock, and never takes it from the caller. The pages of the rules and the dates are the pages for people that rulec and koyomi draw, as they draw them.

### `kind` of `read_order`

- Written: `kind = halves(first: principal.first, second: principal.second).answer`
- Computed by `rulec "tests/mutants/fixtures/halves.rule" output answer`, from `principal.first` and `principal.second`.
- Its values: `odd_half` and `other`; Cedar is given the strings `"odd_half"` and `"other"`.

## Roles

- `clerk`: Answers customers.

Whether a principal holding one role alone (and the roles it includes) is allowed each action: always, in every combination of the rest; sometimes, allowed in some combinations and denied in others; never, denied in every one. `-` is an action that does not take the principal's type. Where a role writes `can`, `sekisho check` holds the actions it is always or sometimes allowed to it.

| principal | `read_order` |
|---|---|
| `User` holding `clerk` | always |
